newsitem.title: UK: Chelsea Village aims for profit in 1998/99.
newsitem.headline: Chelsea Village aims for profit in 1998/99.

text.p: Chelsea Village Plc expects to begin to show a bottom-line profit from 1998/99 once it completes the multi-million pound redevelopment of its Stamford Bridge stadium, chairman Ken Bates said on Friday.
"We would think that we would be showing a profit the year after next," Bates told journalists.
Chelsea Village, owners of English premier league soccer club Chelsea, plan to complete the construction of a new south stand, with club shop, hotels and apartment later this year.
It hopes to commence work on a new west stand this summer, although that remains subject to detailed planning approval.
The club earlier reported a loss of 404,000 pounds in the six months to December 31, 1996. It had a net operating profit before transfer fees and interest of 212,000.
Chelsea have signed a host ot top foreign stars such as Italians Gianluca Vialli, Roberto di Matteo and Gianfranco Zola plus Frenchman Franck Leboeuf.
Bates said that the club had spent 12.5 million on players so far this year but recouped around six million pounds through the sale of less celebrated talents.
The capacity of the Stamford Bridge stadium will rise 20 percent to 35,000 next season when the south stand opens.
Bates said the 160-bedroom Chelsea Village hotel would open for business in December.
He said leading brands such as Hilton and Travelodge had approached the company about partnerships to run the hotel but Chelsea had turned them down.

Bates said the funding was already in place for the 30 million pound south stand development. The west stand is expected to cost a further 20/25 million pounds and Bates said this would be funded by a mixture of debt and equity.
Chelsea hope to enhance their merchandising revenue greatly by opening a new club shop at the ground this summer.
The current club shop is a converted antique store run by an outside group. Bates said that Chelsea were entitled only to a 10 percent fee on its turnover of around two million pounds.
Bates said Chelsea was spending 930,000 pounds on fitting out the new store.
